procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered before applying for a certificate of origin; registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade requires the applicant to prepare proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade requires the applicant to complete the online application form, upload the required documents, and pay the certificate fee.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for this shipment (invoice value up to AED 100,000).
The Ministry of Foreign Trade processes the application, which takes about one working day, and issues the certificate or returns it with comments for correction.
The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of export; it must bear the authorised signature and official seal.
The certificate is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and for only one import; it may list several products.

The exporter must ensure the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar.
The exporter must indicate third-party invoicing if the invoice is issued by a third party.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed.
The Indian importer keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing and must answer a customs request within ten working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.
A certificate issued retrospectively (up to 12 months from shipment) must be marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.
An issued certificate can be amended once for a fee of AED 20; the invoice amount and destination cannot be changed.

caveats.note: The estimate is based on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not specify whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The de minimis tolerance helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the value-addition percentage.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating; the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.
The certificate of origin must be issued before, at, or within five working days of export; it is valid for twelve months and for only one import.
India's certificate form uses box 9 for retrospective issue remarks, while the agreement says box 8; India's form governs entry into India.
The exporter must keep origin records for at least five years under CEPA, even though UAE law sets a shorter three-year minimum.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate of origin for India.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources, not the official text.
The Social Welfare Surcharge is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found), and anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
